alphas.name: Platform
alphas.description: The unified system of automation tools, execution engines, state management backends, module registries, CI/CD pipelines, and integrations that provide the technical foundation for managing infrastructure through code. Includes control nodes/servers (Ansible control nodes, Puppet servers, Terraform Cloud workspaces, Chef servers, Salt masters), their configurations, and the operational infrastructure supporting automated provisioning and configuration management.

narratives.name: Architecture Selection Context
narratives.description: Context for AAP 2.7 architecture selection decisions.

narrativeContexts.context: Organization decides to adopt Red Hat Ansible Automation Platform 2.7 for enterprise infrastructure automation.
AAP 2.7 requires containerized-only deployment, and the team must choose between growth topology (single VM) and enterprise topology (multi-VM with external PostgreSQL and HAProxy).
Architecture review selects deployment model based on scale requirements, identifies RHEL 9.6+ hosting, and plans platform gateway as unified entry point for all AAP services.

narratives.name: Platform Lifecycle
narratives.description: Lifecycle narrative for the automation platform infrastructure.

narrativeContexts.context: AAP 2.7 exclusively supports containerized deployment, requiring selection between growth topology (single VM) and enterprise topology (separate VMs for gateway, controller, hub, EDA, execution nodes with external PostgreSQL and HAProxy).
Platform gateway is deployed as the sole entry point, with containerized installer managing rootless Podman containers on RHEL 9.6+ or operator-based deployment on OpenShift 4.14-4.22.
Platform operates with centralized authentication through gateway, distributed job execution through automation mesh, and continuous monitoring of backend service health and performance.
Platform evolves through sequential upgrades, high availability expansion, performance tuning based on telemetry, and progressive hardening of security posture.

citationNames: Red Hat Ansible Automation Platform 2.7 Documentation

narratives.name: Platform Foundation Overview
narratives.description: Lifecycle narrative for the platform foundation practice.

narrativeContexts.context: Organizations select containerized deployment topology (growth or enterprise) for AAP 2.7, designing platform gateway as unified entry point with authentication, API routing, and RBAC across controller, hub, and EDA controller services.

Platform engineers deploy gateway and controller as rootless Podman containers on RHEL 9.6+, build custom execution environments using ansible-builder or Visual EE Builder, and configure automation mesh with hop and execution nodes spanning hybrid cloud infrastructure.

Production workloads execute through distributed mesh topology with dynamic inventory discovering cloud infrastructure resources, while platform gateway centralizes authentication and API routing across all platform services.

Mesh topology expands to new regions, execution environment images are optimized for size and security, inventory sync performance is tuned, and platform gateway high availability ensures continuous access.

narratives.name: Automation Mesh Maturity
narratives.description: Maturity progression for automation mesh topology.

narrativeContexts.context: Initial deployment co-locates execution nodes with the controller on a single site, distributing jobs across a local pool with basic capacity management and instance group organization.
Hop nodes bridge network boundaries using Receptor protocol on port 27199, enabling execution nodes in remote datacenters and cloud regions to register through TLS/mTLS-encrypted relay paths.

Globally distributed mesh spans continents with latency-based routing, automatic failover, edge location support, and comprehensive telemetry providing visibility into distributed execution health across hybrid infrastructure.

narratives.name: Inventory Source Maturity
narratives.description: Maturity progression for inventory source management.

narrativeContexts.context: Teams begin with static inventories of manually entered hostnames organized into functional groups, sufficient for initial automation targeting but unsustainable as infrastructure scales beyond manual tracking.

Dynamic inventory plugins auto-discover cloud infrastructure from provider APIs (AWS EC2, Azure RM, VMware vCenter), with constructed inventory grouping hosts by metadata attributes using Jinja2 templates.

Smart inventories aggregate hosts from multiple discovery sources into a unified view with duplicate resolution, automated pruning of decommissioned hosts, and performance-optimized sync caching for large-scale infrastructure estates.

personas.name: Platform Engineer
personas.description: Designs, deploys, and operates automation platform infrastructure.

narratives.name: Platform Engineer Role
narratives.description: Role context for the platform engineer persona.

narrativeContexts.context: Enterprise requires production-grade automation platform with hybrid cloud distributed execution, centralized authentication, and governed runtime environments.
Deploy and configure AAP 2.7 with platform gateway, automation mesh spanning multiple datacenters, custom execution environments, and dynamic inventory integration.
Select enterprise topology, deploy containerized platform using rootless Podman, configure gateway with SSO integration, build mesh with hop nodes, establish EE build pipeline.
Operational automation platform with distributed execution, certified runtimes, automated infrastructure discovery, and centralized governance through platform gateway.

personas.name: Cloud Operations Engineer
personas.description: Manages cloud infrastructure integration and dynamic inventory sources.

narratives.name: Cloud Operations Engineer Role
narratives.description: Role context for the cloud operations engineer persona.

narrativeContexts.context: Organization operates infrastructure across multiple cloud providers and on-premises datacenters requiring unified visibility and automated management.
Configure dynamic inventory plugins for each cloud provider, establish constructed grouping logic, and aggregate into unified smart inventories.
Integrate AWS EC2, Azure RM, VMware vCenter, and Kubernetes inventory plugins with appropriate credentials, sync schedules, and metadata enrichment.
Unified multi-source inventory provides real-time visibility into all managed infrastructure assets with automated grouping and stale host pruning.

personaGroups.name: Platform Engineering Team
personaGroups.description: Team deploying and operating the automation platform infrastructure.

activities.name: Deploy AAP Gateway and Controller
activities.description: Install and configure platform gateway with automation controller on target infrastructure.

narratives.name: Gateway and Controller Deployment
narratives.description: Lifecycle for deploying AAP gateway and controller.

narrativeContexts.context: Select deployment topology (growth single-VM or enterprise multi-VM) and plan platform gateway placement as unified entry point for all AAP interactions.
Deploy containerized installer on RHEL 9.6+ using rootless Podman, configure platform gateway with TLS, identity provider integration (LDAP, SAML, OIDC, TACACS+), and API routing to backend services.
Validate gateway routing to controller (/api/v2/), hub (/api/galaxy/), EDA (/api/eda/), apply subscription manifest, configure audit logging, and verify authentication workflows.
Deploy high availability with multiple gateway instances behind HAProxy, configure monitoring and health check endpoints, and establish backup procedures using setup.sh.

citationNames: Red Hat Ansible Automation Platform 2.7 Documentation
AAP 2.7 What's New

activities.name: Build Custom Execution Environments
activities.description: Create containerized ansible runtimes with specialized collection dependencies.

narratives.name: Custom EE Build Process
narratives.description: Lifecycle for building custom execution environments.

narrativeContexts.context: Identify required ansible content collections, Python dependencies, and system packages for custom execution environment definitions.
Build custom EEs using ansible-builder CLI with execution-environment.yml or Visual EE Builder UI, executing four-stage process (Base, Galaxy, Builder, Final) to produce optimized container images.
Publish EE images to container registry (Quay, automation hub), reference from job templates, and integrate CVE scanning with remediation SLAs.
Apply digital signatures for content verification, optimize image layering across variants, automate rebuilds on security patches, and monitor usage analytics for deprecation decisions.

citationNames: Automation Execution Environments Overview

activities.name: Configure Mesh Topology
activities.description: Deploy and connect mesh nodes forming distributed execution network.

narratives.name: Mesh Topology Configuration
narratives.description: Lifecycle for configuring automation mesh topology.

narrativeContexts.context: Plan mesh topology identifying hop node placement in intermediate network zones, execution node co-location with target infrastructure, and node type selection (hybrid, control, execution, hop).
Deploy Receptor instances on hop nodes with TLS/mTLS certificates, register execution nodes through hop relays, configure instance groups organizing nodes by capability or location.
Validate cross-site job execution with acceptable latency, test failover during network partitions, verify FIPS compliance where required, and load test concurrent job capacity.
Expand mesh to new regions, implement latency-based routing, add edge location nodes for IoT automation, and configure telemetry for global execution health visibility.

citationNames: Automation Mesh Explained: Scalability for Hybrid Cloud

activities.name: Integrate Dynamic Inventory Sources
activities.description: Configure cloud provider inventory plugins for automated host discovery.

narratives.name: Dynamic Inventory Integration
narratives.description: Lifecycle for integrating dynamic inventory sources.

narrativeContexts.context: Identify cloud provider inventory plugins needed (AWS EC2, Azure RM, GCP, VMware vCenter, Kubernetes) and plan credential configuration for API access.
Configure inventory sources in controller with provider credentials, sync schedules, filtering rules, and variable enrichment mapping cloud metadata to ansible variables.
Validate host discovery, configure constructed inventory plugins for dynamic grouping by metadata attributes (OS, datacenter, VLAN), and monitor sync failures with alerting.
Aggregate multiple sources into smart inventories, implement duplicate host resolution, optimize caching for large environments, and automate pruning of stale hosts.

citationNames: How to Use Dynamic Inventories in Ansible Automation
Guide to Multi-Homed Inventory Management

activities.name: Baseline Platform Configuration
activities.description: Establish routing configuration, data store design, and baseline platform settings.

narratives.name: Baseline Configuration Context
narratives.description: Context for establishing baseline platform configuration.

narrativeContexts.context: The platform architecture has been selected with deployment topology and hosting platform decisions documented.
Platform gateway routing paths, PostgreSQL shared data store configuration, TLS certificate management, and Configuration as Code approach remain undefined.

Define platform gateway API routing configuration, configure external PostgreSQL for enterprise topology, establish TLS certificate management, and select Configuration as Code tooling for programmatic management.

citationNames: Red Hat Ansible Automation Platform 2.7 Documentation

activities.name: Evolve Platform Infrastructure
activities.description: Upgrade, harden, and continuously improve platform components.

narratives.name: Platform Evolution Cycle
narratives.description: Continuous improvement cycle for platform infrastructure.

narrativeContexts.context: Identify platform upgrade path (2.5 to 2.6 to 2.7), plan gateway high availability expansion, and evaluate telemetry for performance optimization opportunities.
Execute sequential upgrades with zero-downtime rolling deployment, deploy additional gateway instances behind load balancer, and implement performance tuning.
Validate upgrade success, confirm gateway request latency and throughput meet targets, verify disaster recovery procedures, and assess security posture.
Document upgrade procedures in runbook, standardize HA deployment pattern, update monitoring dashboards, and plan next improvement cycle.

citationNames: Red Hat Ansible Automation Platform 2.7 Documentation

activities.name: Decommission Automation Platform
activities.description: Systematically retire platform components with workload migration.

narratives.name: Platform Decommission Context
narratives.description: Context for platform decommissioning decisions.

narrativeContexts.context: The automation platform has served its purpose and a replacement or consolidation decision has been made.
Active workloads, inventory data, credentials, and job history must be preserved or migrated before platform components can be safely removed.
Execute decommission runbook: migrate workloads to replacement platform, export critical data, drain mesh nodes, remove containers, clean up certificates and credentials.

citationNames: Red Hat Ansible Automation Platform 2.7 Documentation

activities.name: Provision Default Execution Environments
activities.description: Pull and validate Red Hat provided execution environments for initial use.

narratives.name: Default EE Provisioning Context
narratives.description: Context for provisioning default execution environments.

narrativeContexts.context: The automation platform is provisioned and ready to execute automation workloads.
Execution environments must be available and validated before job templates can run, and the team needs to understand default EE contents and limitations.
Pull default EE images from Red Hat registry, cache locally, validate job template execution against default EEs, document contents, and identify dependency gaps requiring custom builds.

citationNames: Automation Execution Environments Overview

activities.name: Optimize EE Distribution
activities.description: Improve execution environment distribution efficiency across mesh infrastructure.

narratives.name: EE Distribution Optimization Context
narratives.description: Context for optimizing execution environment distribution.

narrativeContexts.context: Execution environments are certified with security scanning and digital signatures, and the platform serves multiple sites and regions.
Image pull latency, registry replication overhead, duplicate content across EE variants, and lifecycle management of obsolete images create operational friction.
Implement multi-site registry replication, optimize image layering to minimize duplication, automate pruning of obsolete versions, and tie EE lifecycle to ansible-core version cadence.

citationNames: Automation Execution Environments Overview

activities.name: Provision Initial Mesh Cluster
activities.description: Deploy initial execution nodes co-located with controller for local distribution.

narratives.name: Initial Mesh Cluster Context
narratives.description: Context for provisioning initial mesh cluster.

narrativeContexts.context: The automation controller is provisioned and ready to distribute execution workloads.
Execution nodes must be registered, instance groups configured, and basic load balancing established before automation can scale beyond the controller host.
Register execution nodes to the controller, configure instance groups organizing nodes by capability, validate job distribution across the local pool, and document network connectivity assumptions.

citationNames: Red Hat Ansible Automation Platform 2.7 Documentation

activities.name: Scale Mesh to Global Distribution
activities.description: Expand automation mesh to global scale with edge locations and latency routing.

narratives.name: Global Mesh Scaling Context
narratives.description: Context for scaling mesh to global distribution.

narrativeContexts.context: Automation mesh is resilient across hybrid cloud with failover tested and compliance validated.
Global-scale automation requires regional execution nodes, latency-based routing, edge location support, and comprehensive distributed telemetry.

Deploy regional execution nodes in 3+ geographic regions, implement latency-based routing, add edge nodes for IoT automation, configure global mesh telemetry, and test disaster recovery for regional failures.

citationNames: Automation Mesh Explained: Scalability for Hybrid Cloud

activities.name: Aggregate Multi-Source Inventories
activities.description: Unify multiple inventory sources into smart inventories with optimization.

narratives.name: Multi-Source Inventory Aggregation Context
narratives.description: Context for aggregating multi-source inventories.

narrativeContexts.context: Multiple cloud provider inventory sources are syncing and constructed groups organize hosts by metadata attributes.
Hosts from different sources may overlap, sync performance degrades at scale, and decommissioned hosts persist as stale entries.
Configure smart inventories aggregating 3+ sources, implement duplicate host resolution, optimize inventory caching, automate stale host pruning, and track sync performance metrics.

citationNames: Guide to Multi-Homed Inventory Management

patterns.description: Coordinated lifecycle from platform architecture through production operations and evolution.

patternViews.description: Architecture definition, topology planning, and initial provisioning.

narrativeContexts.context: Select containerized deployment topology (growth or enterprise), plan platform gateway as unified entry point, provision initial execution nodes co-located with controller, pull default EEs, and populate initial static inventory with known hosts.

patternViews.name: Build
patternViews.description: Platform provisioning, mesh extension, and dynamic integration.

narrativeContexts.context: Deploy platform gateway and controller as rootless Podman containers, configure platform baseline settings and routing, extend mesh to multi-site with hop nodes, build custom EEs via ansible-builder, and integrate dynamic inventory plugins for cloud infrastructure discovery.

patternViews.name: Run
patternViews.description: Production operations, governance, and steady-state management.

narrativeContexts.context: Platform operates at production scale with hybrid cloud resilient mesh, certified execution environments with CVE scanning and digital signatures, constructed inventory grouping hosts by metadata, and gateway providing unified access with monitoring and health checks.

patternViews.name: Optimize
patternViews.description: Continuous improvement, global scaling, and lifecycle evolution.

narrativeContexts.context: Platform evolves through sequential upgrades with zero-downtime deployment, mesh scales globally with latency-based routing and edge support, EE distribution is optimized with registry replication and image layering, and multi-source smart inventories provide unified infrastructure visibility.
